The existing fire protection and fire alarm systems are to remain as existing and will be unchanged, 4.) No changes in building egress shall occur, 5.) Re:  Flat roof approximately 37X25.  We propose the following 10 year Carlisle roofing system:
Strip off existing roof system.  Clean all loose debris from roof.  Install 1- inch poly-urethane insulation board with an r-factor of approximately 5.6 (not the 1/2–inch recovery board that has no R-factor rating and which we in the field have found to be substandard) over roof area and screw down using disks and screws.  Lay out .060 rubber roof membrane, cutting out all protrusions as we go, such as: soil pipes, penthouses, skylights, etc.  Fold back rubber, apply bonding adhesive to both insulation and to rubber membrane.  Wait until tacky, about 15 minutes.  Then fold rubber over insulation to form a tight seal.  
-	Install pre-molded vent pipe boots to vent pipes where possible.  
-	Rubber flash all chimneys, skylights, and protrusions on roof with rubber flashing.  
-	Install a pressure treated wood edge nailer.  Install .032 heavy gauge metal to outside edges of roof and seal all nails with rubber edge flashing.  
-	Install R.U.S.S. strip where needed at any transitions to prevent bridging.
-	Where drains exist, install copper sleeve in drain and seal as needed.  
-	Clean all debris from job site.  
The above work will carry a ten year contractor’s warranty on labor and materials under normal wear and tear.

-	Re: All electrical and a.c. conduit, at least 14 of them. We will install 14-15 new securement plates/fasteners. (We are not responsible if the existing fasteners break due to their age.)

Replace 2 existing Andersen single pane wood casement windows with 2 Harvey Majesty casement windows of the same size. The Harvey Majesty casement windows are energy star rated with an STC of 40. The intent is to lessen the noise from Jet Aircraft taking off and landing at Logan Airport. The existing casement windows are located in the east facing wall of the 1st floor kitchen. The kitchen is currently being renovated under Boston Inspectional Services Department Permit Number SF371622. 

The proposed work will proceed as follows:

1.	Replace 2 existing Andersen single pane wood casement windows with 2 new construction Harvey Majesty casement windows. The Harvey Majesty windows will be made to fit the existing rough opening. The exterior nailing flange will be sealed with Harvey peal and stick rubber as per the Harvey window installation instructions. The existing vinyl siding will be re-installed.
2.	Apply non-expanding foam insulation between the existing rough opening and the new casement windows.
3.	Insulate the wall cavities around the two new casement windows with ROXUL rock wool insulation (R-13). 
4.	Cover the ROXUL rock wool insulation with a 4 mil polyethylene vapor barrier stapled to the existing studs. Tape seams as required. 
5.	Replace the existing Plaster Board (Blue Board) with 1 layer of ½” Homasote 440 Sound Board under 1 layer of ½” Plaster Board.  Apply skin coat of plaster to the new blue board to match existing kitchen walls. The existing wall board was installed over the old lathes the Homasote and blue board combination will be the same thickness as the old wall.

There is an existing fence at the rear of the property that was constructed in 2012 by the developer without a permit. This work was done prior to our purchase of the property. 

We are now applying for a permit for the fence. We are happy with the current design, but recognize it covers a "right of way". Our permit application and proposal includes a modification that will not interfere with the "right of way" our neighbor at 12 Monument Court has over the property. Specifically, the proposed fence design would remove two sections of fence and replace with a small section of fence along the street and a gate. This would provide privacy from the street, yet keep open the area designated as a "right of way". It also keeps clear the easement area in the alley and alongside 12 Monument Court.

We have included plans for current and proposed design. We have also included photos of the original chain link fence (photo from 2011), which was in place prior to the new fence going up, and our modification more closely matches that design, although offers an improvement in terms of durability and appearance.

This proposal is in response to a violation notice we received and attempts to respond to that letter, the "right of way" issue, and at the same time minimize any unnecessary construction or demolition on the property.

Weston & Sampson Engineers, Inc. (Weston & Sampson) has been retained by Leers Weinzapfel Associates Architects to complete a geotechnical evaluation for the proposed East Boston Police Station at 338 East Eagle Street and 0 (Zero) Condor Street in Boston, Massachusetts. Our evaluation will include nine (9) test borings to investigate subsurface conditions at the site. The test borings will be observed by a Weston & Sampson representative and completed by New England Boring Contractors of Brockton, Massachusetts. 

The test borings will be advanced with a truck-mounted drill rig using hollow-stem auger and drive-and-wash drilling methods to depths up to 50 feet. Standard Penetration Tests will be conducted in the borings at approximate 5-ft. intervals to obtain geotechnical samples and evaluate in-situ soil consistencies. Upon completion, the boreholes will be backfilled with the cuttings removed during drilling and patched to match surrounding surfaces (e.g. concrete or asphalt). No groundwater monitoring wells will be installed.
